subject: Shadowridge: AZ1 token choke causing end-user timeouts — urgent routing authorization
messages:
From: Priya Sutherland <priya@shadowridge.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and elevated p99 latency from around 08:50 PDT in our US-EAST-1 (AZ1) zone. This is impacting checkout for ~8% of sessions (replay attached). Errors look like token validation failures + upstream 502s from your inference endpoint. Our customers are reporting timeouts.

Attached: traffic_snapshot-20270411.csv (sampled request logs, headers redacted).

Can Redwood perform a cross-region shift while you investigate? We need an ETA and any temporary mitigation you can put in place (canary redirect, rate-limits, or model pin to a lower-latency variant). This is P0 for us.

Priya Sutherland
Head of SRE, Shadowridge
priya@shadowridge.com
+1 415-555-0192

On behalf of: Ethan Lowe, CTO <ethan@shadowridge.com>
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Priya Sutherland <priya@shadowridge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

Thanks Priya — sorry for the disruption. I’m escalating to our on-call infra + routing leads now. Quick answers up front:
- We can push a traffic-steward/redirect to route Shadowridge traffic from us-east-1 (AZ1) to us-west-2 within ~20 minutes if you authorize.
- We’ll hold a canary at 5% for 10 minutes, then increase if stable.
- We’ll prepare a temporary SLA amendment and credit proposal while we investigate root cause.

Marcus / Hannah — can you give an initial read on whether this looks like a KV-cache/token mismatch (from the traces) vs. an AZ network amplification? I’ve attached their CSV for quick triage.

Priya — please confirm immediate authorization to perform the cross-region diversion and whether you want service continuity only (no config changes) or a combined diversion + model pin to the quantized xform-small variant.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

Investigating — initial telemetry: we’re seeing KV cache eviction spikes and a sustained increase in 429/502 combos originating from the AZ1 long-tail pool. Not a customer-side token format issue; looks internal to the shard.

Mitigation proposal (safe order):
1) Approve immediate traffic shift: steward 5% -> 20% over 15m -> 100% to us-west-2 (us) if no errors. This avoids a broad model reload.
2) Pin Shadowridge to the non-quantized variant in the destination region for 4 hours to avoid transient perf regressions; revert after verification.
3) Open a P1 incident to kernel/runtime team for KV-cache hotspot (Triage owner: marcus_lin).

If we shift, we’ll ask for exec-level authorization for cross-region failover (customer-facing shift + brief SLA note). Also recommend offering a 10% credit for downtime minutes > 5 in the timeframe per contract.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

I support Marcus’s plan. Operational notes:
- We have capacity in us-west-2 (reserved pool) and a pre-warmed path for Shadowridge instances.
- Network egress and regional routing policies will be updated; estimated change window 18 minutes from approval.

Monica — pushing to exec: do you want me to start the steward (5% canary) while we wait for formal sign-off, or hold until you get explicit customer OK?

I’ll prep the runnable runbook and add the traffic diversion entries to PagerDuty incident PDT-58291.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Priya Sutherland <priya@shadowridge.com>, Ethan Lowe <ethan@shadowridge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

Priya / Ethan — thank you for the quick report and sample logs. Per internal triage, we will:
- Begin a cross-region traffic steward to us-west-2 now (canary 5% -> 20% -> 100%). Estimated completion: 10:30 PDT.
- Pin to the non-quantized model variant in the destination region for 4 hours.
- Prepare a temporary SLA amendment and 10% credit draft; attached for your review (temporary-sla-amendment-draft.pdf).

Attached: proposed-routing-change-plan.pdf (includes rollback steps, timing, and comms). I’ve copied the PagerDuty incident and the runbook.

Please reply with a one-line approval ("approve shift now") so we can execute. If we don’t hear back in 10 minutes we will proceed with the canary per our emergency playbook and notify you immediately.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 650-555-0118
From: Priya Sutherland <priya@shadowridge.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan@shadowridge.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained 5xx + checkout timeouts from AZ1 — seeing token churn

Monica / team,

Thanks — we saw error volume drop dramatically after your canary kicked off (~10:07 PDT). The attach snapshot matches what we observed; checkout errors reduced to <0.2% across sessions. Appreciate the quick pivot and the temporary SLA draft — we’ll review and sign.

We’d like a short post-mortem once the root cause is confirmed and a timeline for any preventive changes to KV-cache policies.

Priya Sutherland
Head of SRE, Shadowridge
